faqs.a: A way for a small business to get its own small AI model for one job, like sorting support tickets or reading invoices. Idle gaming PCs and laptops do the training, and you pay only if the model passes your test.

faqs.q: How much data do I need?
faqs.a: Between 20 and 50 examples of the right answer. Some are kept aside, unseen, to test the model before you pay.
Hindi, Hinglish and English. Two of the first five jobs, support tickets and clinic questions, are built around Hinglish.

faqs.q: What if the model isn't good enough?
faqs.a: Then you don't pay. It has to pass your test and beat the untrained model; if it misses either, the whole budget is refunded automatically.

faqs.q: Can I use it for my business today?
faqs.a: Not yet for real money. Ekido runs on a public test network with test money until an independent audit.

verify.title: Verify this payout
verify.lead: Your browser reads the verdict from a chain transaction and checks it against checkpoint and provider details supplied by the coordinator.
verify.recording: A recording can't be checked against a chain: the chain it ran on is gone. Switch to live, run a job to the end, then come back here.
verify.offlineTitle: Not available: the coordinator is offline
verify.offline: The check needs the job details from the coordinator. Mission control shows how to start it, or lets you watch the recording.
verify.notSettledTitle: Not available yet: no settled job
verify.notSettled: This check runs once the newest job is paid out on-chain. Start a job on mission control and let it finish.
verify.notYet: Nothing has been checked yet. It takes a few seconds and sends no transactions.
verify.withdrawalSubtitle: Read-only check against the configured chain and escrow. A withdrawal can combine credits from several jobs.
verify.withdrawalOk: The configured escrow emitted a withdrawal of {amount} token units (6 decimals) to {wallet} in block {block}. This does not identify which job funded those credits.

limits.training: That the training itself ran as claimed. Payment rests on the quality test, not on a proof of execution.
limits.verifiers: That the verifiers were honest. They're run by our team, so a quorum of them could sign a bad result.
limits.details: That checkpoint steps, signers, provider wallets or prices are authentic. The coordinator supplies those details; coordinated changes can make an incorrect payout appear consistent.
limits.escrow: That the configured escrow address is trustworthy. Check it independently before relying on the contract identity check.
limits.contents: What's inside the checkpoints or quality reports. These checks do not open or authenticate their contents.
limits.split: The current verifier workers also trust the coordinator's proposed payout split.
limits.rpc: This reads through one RPC node. A careful checker would use their own.

chain.title: On-chain ledger
chain.lead: Your browser reads this page straight from {chain} (chain {id}). It never asks our coordinator. The money is test USDC held by our escrow contract, and anyone can check the same numbers on Basescan.
chain.readFallback: The chain could not be read.
chain.errorDetail: {error} Public RPCs sometimes limit requests, so wait a moment and try again.
chain.waiting: Your browser reads the escrow's whole history from {chain}'s public servers, about 150 requests. Start it when you want to check: nothing is read until you do.
chain.progress: Reading the escrow's history from its deploy block, 50,000 blocks at a time
chain.reservesSubtitle: What the escrow holds, against everything it has promised to pay
chain.withdrawOnly: Money leaves only when the person it's owed to calls withdraw(). Nobody else can move it, us included.
chain.contractsSubtitle: Deployed on Base Sepolia on 7 Nov 2026
chain.escrowWhat: Holds budgets, checks verifier signatures, pays out
chain.registryWhat: Public sign-up for providers, holds no money
chain.unaudited: Unaudited and testnet only. It enforces who gets paid. It does not prove the training happened, which is the Quality Guard's job.
chain.reconciliationIndex: Three independent sources must agree: the replayed events, the contract's own totals, and each wallet's balance. Event history came from our index in one request and passed these checks; if it hadn't, your browser would have scanned the chain itself.
chain.reconciliationChain: Three independent sources must agree: the replayed events, the contract's own totals, and each wallet's balance. Event history was scanned straight from the chain.

help.metaDescription: How to rent out a GPU, submit a job, check a payout on-chain, and what every badge means.
help.title: Help
help.intro: Answers to the common questions, what each badge means, and the words we use.

what.q: What is Ekido, in one line?
what.a: A network where a training job survives its GPU dying, bad results get refused, and an escrow contract pays each provider only for the work that made it into the final model.

blockchain.q: Why does it need a blockchain?
blockchain.a: A client and a provider who don't know each other need someone neutral to hold the money and follow the agreed rules, even if we disappear. The escrow contract is that neutral party: the budget is locked before work starts, and it pays out only with verifier signatures. You can check all of it yourself on the <chain>On-chain page</chain>. It doesn't make the computing itself trustworthy. That's what the Quality Guard is for.

money.a: No. Everything runs on Base Sepolia, a test network, with test USDC that has no value. Never send real funds.

rent.q: How do I rent out my GPU?
rent.a: Open <provide>Provide compute</provide>, set a name and a price per step, and copy the one command it shows. It creates a provider key on your machine, registers your device, and starts taking work. It works on an NVIDIA GPU or on a CPU.

paid.a: After a job settles, your share sits in the escrow under your wallet. Call withdraw() on the escrow from that wallet whenever you like. Type your address into "Check any wallet" on the On-chain page to see what you're owed.

dropout.q: What happens if my GPU drops out halfway?
dropout.a: The coordinator notices, blocks your old worker from writing, and moves the job to another provider from the last trusted checkpoint. You're still paid for your accepted steps up to that checkpoint.

nothing.q: Why did a provider earn nothing?
nothing.a: Either its work was refused by the Quality Guard, or it never saved a checkpoint that was accepted. Only accepted steps are paid.

disagree.q: What if I disagree with a payout?
disagree.a: The client can dispute during the dispute window by posting a bond. The arbiter decides. If the arbiter stays silent for 3 days, the verdict stands and the bond is returned.

custom.q: Can I run my own training code?
custom.a: Not yet. Only approved workload templates run today, to protect providers' machines. Sandboxed custom code is on the roadmap.

real.name: Real GPU
real.means: A physical GPU doing the work live.

separate.name: Real, separate machine
separate.means: A physical GPU on another computer, often a teammate's.

capped.name: Capped profile
capped.means: The same physical GPU with a memory limit, to show the job adapting to a smaller card.

fault.name: Injected fault
fault.means: A provider we made misbehave on purpose, to show bad work being refused.

recorded.name: Recorded
recorded.means: Played back from a saved real run, not happening now.

local.name: Local chain
local.means: Settled on a chain running on this laptop, not on Base Sepolia.

synthetic.name: Synthetic
synthetic.means: A small CPU workload standing in when the GPU isn't available.

escrow.means: The contract that holds a job's budget until the verdict decides who gets what.

verifier.means: An independent process that evaluates the model and signs the verdict. 2 of 3 must agree.

checkpoint.means: A saved copy of the training state. A job resumes from the last accepted one.

step.means: One unit of training that means the same on every GPU, however it's split into smaller batches.

fencing.means: A counter that stops an old, disconnected worker from writing after the job moved on.

window.means: The time after a verdict when the client can still challenge it.

reserves.means: A live check that the escrow holds at least as much USDC as it owes.

trouble.coordinator: "Coordinator offline": the scheduling server isn't reachable. Switch to the recorded run from the top bar, or check Status.
trouble.chain: "Chain unreachable": the public Base Sepolia RPC is limiting requests. Wait a few seconds and read again.
trouble.provider: A provider command fails: it needs Python 3.12 and the Ekido agent installed. The page shows the exact command for this network.
trouble.keys: Keyboard shortcuts: press ? on the dashboard to see them.
